world_change: In Bangladesh, rising heat has moved from an episodic weather hazard into a persistent labour, health, household and economic constraint, while new 2026 evidence shows that practical cooling and social-protection responses can reduce part of the burden.

evidence_basis.claim: National analysis using 16,000+ people found rising heat associated with physical and mental health effects and about 250 million lost workdays in 2024.
Survey of 175 Dhaka informal-worker households measured missed work, income loss, health burden and impacts at work and home.
Year-long evidence from eight Dhaka-region apparel factories and three dozen worker homes found a seven-month heat-stress season and quantified cooling economics.
Worker interviews in two Dhaka garment factories documented headaches, dizziness, fatigue, nausea, absenteeism, productivity effects and barriers to hydration/cooling.
Bangladesh heatwaves contributed to nationwide school closures and child health/learning disruption in 2024.

human_emotional_hook.basis: Heat follows people across the boundary between earning a living and recovering at home: workers can lose income by stopping, but continued exposure carries health and exhaustion costs; children and families face parallel heat burdens.
human_emotional_hook.boundary: Use evidenced worker/household experiences or clearly labelled fiction grounded in those conditions. Do not invent a named real worker or attribute a surveyed experience to an invented individual as fact.
